recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source change is needed for FHIR-13916 unless a future work-group decision explicitly requires a Subscription-specific HTTP status code beyond the standard create interaction rules.
issue_request: FHIR-13916 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification STU3 change request asking what a server should do when a posted Subscription cannot be honored at all, such as because the channel type or criteria are unsupported. The approved resolution was to document returning an error OperationOutcome as a recommended option, not to mandate the suggested 412 status code.
initial_application: Commit 8efdf4db313c7d7a828d5f5cfdeca3a9fde3bb9d applied GF#13916 by adding Subscription notes that say a server SHOULD check whether it is prepared to accept/process the subscription and, if not, SHOULD return an OperationOutcome error instead of processing the create. Later Subscription refactors, including ef0558f0c6008b9fd15ed93c302b484ab1c67f10 and d51aae543ee91023d3a373ffba704fee0904f8c0, preserved the guidance in the active Subscriptions framework page.
additional_context: Subscription and the Subscriptions framework page are active in the current build. Current source also lists concrete processing checks for supported topics, filters, channel type, endpoint, and payload. The later Applied issue FHIR-47808 asked a closely related R6 ballot question about failed Subscription creation HTTP codes; it was applied and is already audited on the combined branch, and the current http.html#create guidance supports normal create failure codes such as 400/422 with OperationOutcome details rather than a Subscription-specific 412 rule.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current source already conveys the FHIR-13916 behavior and a source edit would duplicate existing framework guidance or conflict with later general HTTP create guidance.
